facts.text: Pine Creek earned its name from the towering pine trees lining its banks, a favorite spot for fly fishers and hikers.
By 1898, homesteaders in Pine Creek had built a one‑room schoolhouse, marking the community’s first organized education.
The Northern Pacific Railway’s arrival after 1883 spurred Pine Creek’s growth, transforming it from a reservation land to a thriving settlement.
During the 1970s and 80s, Pine Creek hosted the Montana Gang, a gathering of writers and musicians who inspired Montana’s literary scene.
The 1946 Pine Creek Lodge, built by Wayne Crosby, remains a rustic stone venue for live music, dining, and mountain‑view lodging.
Pine Creek lies where the creek meets the Yellowstone River, a point where waters from the Absaroka Mountains enter the valley.
